Newport News charges $1.18 per $100 of assessed value for 2025-26. That rate has held since 2023-24. Before that it was $1.20 for 2021-22 and 2022-23, and $1.22 from 2013-14 through 2020-21. The city assesses at 100 percent of value, so the rate applies to the full assessed figure. City Council sets the rate, not the Assessor.

Citywide assessments rose about 4.2 percent from 2024-25 to 2025-26, so many owners saw their values move. The Assessor's website has a tax calculator you can use to estimate a bill for your own parcel. Treat the result as an estimate, since it is not a quote.

Value and billing sit in different hands. Every parcel is reassessed annually by the Real Estate Assessor, and the new figure takes effect the next July 1. Money flows through the City Treasurer. The Commissioner of the Revenue handles relief programs and supports the Board of Review.

  • Real Estate Assessor: 700 Town Center Drive, Suite 220, phone 757-926-1926, email restate@nnva.gov.
  • Treasurer: P.O. Box 975, Newport News, VA 23607, phone 757-926-8731, email treasurer@nnva.gov.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 2400 Washington Avenue, phone 757-926-8752.

Bills are normally due December 5 and June 5. If you improve the land, say with an addition, the city may send a supplemental bill. Some bills also carry a stormwater fee. If you pay through online banking, enter the grand total for the account number.

Disagreements over value go to the Board of Review. Hearings take place between September 1 and November 30, and judges of the Newport News Circuit Court name the members each year. Applications are accepted July 1 through September 1, and the city grants no extensions.

  • Weekend rule: if September 1 lands on a weekend or holiday, the next business day is the deadline.
  • Late filings: anything postmarked or hand delivered after the deadline is rejected.
  • Mailing caution: since December 24, 2025, a USPS postmark shows the date the mail was processed, which can be later than the day you dropped it off. Hand delivery or an early mailing is safer.
  • Questions: the Board's administrative assistant, 757-812-7816.

Residential and commercial appeals use different forms. A procedures document for the 2026 cycle and a letter of authorization for agents are posted on the city's Board of Review page. Before the deadline, ask the Assessor for an informal review of your value. That conversation costs nothing and sometimes settles the question.

sections.h2: What buyers ask about Newport News
sections.html:
Newport News had 186,247 residents in 2020. It lies along the James River's north shore at the point where the river opens into Hampton Roads, and 42 percent of its area is water, at an elevation of 15 feet. Prospective buyers often want to know if a home is near a creek, an inlet or a mapped flood zone. Find that out before they ask.

Voters in Warwick and Newport News chose in 1958 to consolidate under one name, so several neighborhoods sit in what used to be the City of Warwick. Shipbuilding, Fort Eustis and the school system anchor local employment, which keeps demand tied to the military and the shipyard.

Unpaid city tax gets first claim on the money from a sale. Under Va. Code 58.1-3340, whoever handles the closing, a buyer or a foreclosure trustee, sends part of the proceeds to the city for taxes and levies plus any penalties and interest. The Treasurer then lifts the lien from the title.

Who owes the current year's share is a contract term, so spell out the split in your agreement. A grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of price also applies under Va. Code 58.1-802, charged to the seller unless the two sides negotiate another arrangement. It is paid at the circuit court clerk's office when the deed is recorded.

The Treasurer keeps a page for real estate auctions of properties with delinquent taxes or liens, with the legal notice and auction flyer. If you see a notice for your own parcel, time is short, and a sale you arrange yourself gives you more control over terms than an auction does.

The Commissioner of the Revenue administers the city's relief programs. They include a real estate tax deferral for the elderly and disabled, an exemption for disabled ex-service members, and deferral and exemption programs for mobile homes. The city also offers a Residential Rehabilitation Property Tax Abatement Program with its own calculator, and the Assessor's site has a VA Deed Alert tool.

Income limits and rules are posted on those pages. For state income and tax relief questions, call 757-926-8653. If no program fits and the house needs more work than you can pay for, a cash sale of the property as is can clear the tax at closing instead.

Begin by requesting a payoff letter from the Treasurer showing the balance, penalties and interest included. Lay it beside your last two bills to see which installments are settled. Next, read the proration clause in your contract. Then make sure the title company has the correct account number, particularly if the bill includes a stormwater fee. Finally, ask the Treasurer's office when records update after payment, since the lien release depends on it.

An as-is cash sale avoids repair negotiations, open houses and a lender's appraisal. Closing still runs through a title company, so a payoff and a settlement statement are part of it. Read both carefully before signing.

Gather a few items before you call the Treasurer or the Assessor: the account number from your bill, the property address, and the name on the deed. If you are calling on behalf of an owner, ask each office what written authorization it wants. The Board of Review page includes a letter of authorization for agents, and the same form is a useful model for other requests. Keep a note of who you spoke with and what each office promised, because a closing can move fast once a contract is signed.

If you plan to appeal and sell in the same year, do not wait. The appeal window closes September 1, and a pending appeal can leave a buyer unsure what the tax will be. Tell your agent and the title company about it so the contract can say who benefits from any reduction.

faqs.q: What is the Newport News property tax rate?
faqs.a: The rate is $1.18 per $100 of assessed value for 2025-26, the same as 2024-25 and 2023-24. City Council sets it each year, so check with the Assessor or Treasurer.

faqs.q: When are Newport News real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are normally due December 5 and June 5. Improvements to the land may produce a supplemental bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Newport News assessment?
faqs.a: Applications to the Board of Review run July 1 through September 1, with no extensions. If September 1 is a weekend or holiday, the next business day is the deadline.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Newport News Treasurer?
faqs.a: Write to P.O. Box 975, Newport News, VA 23607, call 757-926-8731 or email treasurer@nnva.gov. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Newport News house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien comes first, so the title company pays the balance from your proceeds and the Treasurer releases the lien. Get a written payoff before closing.
